note: claude-opus-5-5、入力 3955 / 出力 659 トークン

data.reason: The KPI asks to deliver as many orders as possible within the promised times, so on_time_deliveries is the primary goal. The KPI also allows revising the promised times, and it requires that a change worse for customers be justified by its measured effect on them. Option 2 judges everything against the SLA, so a looser SLA would look like a pure gain. That makes the required customer-impact measurement impossible. Option 3 moves the main objective away from the stated goal. Option 1 keeps the stated goal and adds SLA-independent monitors (p95_wait_s, max_wait_s, unfinished). These are the measurements needed before accepting any contract change. For now, 'worse for customers' means any increase in p95_wait_s, max_wait_s or unfinished. No numeric guard values are set because the KPI gives no levels. Fairness between companies is not part of the KPI as written.
assumptions: p95_wait_s and max_wait_s measure order-to-delivery time independently of the SLA definition.
Measurements with the same seeds and demand are comparable across amendments.
The KPI is town-wide and does not require per-company fairness.
unknowns: The current baseline values of on_time_deliveries, p95_wait_s, max_wait_s and unfinished under the rules in force.
Whether the operator has implicit hard limits on customer wait times.
How on-time performance is spread among companies A, B and C.

follow_ups.text: Measure the rules in force to establish a baseline for the chosen KPI metrics.
Should a hard upper limit on p95_wait_s or max_wait_s be set as a guard once baseline values are known?
